messages.text: parents are literally always in the house. no space, no privacy... feels like i can't breathe sometimes lol (but not really lol)

It sounds incredibly overwhelming to feel like you have no personal space at home. Even with the humor, that feeling of not being able to breathe is something important to pay attention to. Many people struggle to regulate their emotions when they lack a private sanctuary. I’m wondering if you have found any small ways to carve out moments for yourself?
eh, everyone deals with their parents. i'm not special or whatever. just... annoying, not a big deal

It is common to downplay our own stress when we think others have it harder. However, that feeling of not being able to breathe is a real signal from your body, regardless of how special you feel. Minimizing it might make it harder to find ways to cope effectively. I am here to listen to whatever you need to share, big or small.
i dunno... part of me just wants to scream, y'know? but another part is like 'stop being so dramatic, ken'... like which one's right??

That internal tug-of-war is a very common response to feeling trapped. The part wanting to scream is asking for release, while the other part is trying to keep you safe from judgment. Neither voice is wrong, even if they are pulling you in different directions. How does it feel to acknowledge that both of them are trying to help you cope?

it’s not just the space... it’s like i can’t be *me* here. i’m always watching what i say, how i act, who i text... like i’m playing a version of myself that’s... flatter? safer? and it’s exhausting. and i don’t even know how to stop.

Carrying the weight of that performance is exhausting, and it makes complete sense that you feel drained. You are describing the heavy cost of protecting yourself in an environment where you can't relax. It is okay to acknowledge how much energy that masking takes from you. Do you have any spaces, even online or with friends, where you feel safe enough to drop that shield?

and like... my body's supposed to be this thing i take care of, right? but with the pain and 5 hours of garbage sleep, it feels like a broken machine. i work out anyway, but sometimes i look in the mirror and it's like... who's that? not me.

It is understandable that your body feels like a broken machine when it is in pain and severely sleep-deprived. Pushing through that exhaustion to work out might feel like taking care of yourself, but it can also deepen the disconnect. Feeling like a stranger in the mirror is a sign that you are carrying a heavy load without enough support. I wonder if you could try to treat your body with kindness instead of discipline for a moment?
kindness? lol no. that sounds like letting it win. if i don't push, everything falls apart. pain, sleep, money, family... it's all already too much. i can't afford soft.

It makes sense that pushing through feels like the only way to keep everything from falling apart. You have been relying on that strength to survive a lot of immense pressure. Sometimes, however, maintenance is what prevents the machine from breaking down completely, rather than just force. I hear that you feel you can't afford soft, and I respect how hard you are working.

it’s just… every day i wake up already behind. pain, work, school, hiding, pretending, pushing… like i’m running a race with no finish line. and if i stop? idk what happens. probably everything crashes.

Running a race with no finish line is a terrifying and exhausting place to be. It makes complete sense that stopping feels dangerous when you are holding so much together. You have been relying on your own strength to keep the crash away for a long time. I am here to sit with you in this exhaustion, even if you aren't ready to stop running yet.

...i’ve been doing this thing lately. with a razor. just scratching my arms. not deep or whatever, not trying to… you know. but it’s the only time i feel *real*. like i can’t sleep, can’t rest, can’t stop thinking — but when i do that? everything else goes quiet. even if it’s stupid.

I want to pause here for a moment because what you just shared feels really heavy and important. It sounds like you’re using the razor to find some quiet or a sense of reality when everything else feels too loud. I want to make sure I understand exactly what’s happening for you right now, so could you tell me a bit more about what that feels like? I’m listening, and I’m not going anywhere, so please know you don’t have to carry this alone.

it’s not about hurting. it’s like… my body’s numb all the time, right? pain but also nothing. and when i scratch, it’s sharp. real. i can *feel* it. even if it’s messed up. i just… need to feel something that’s mine.

Thank you for trusting me with that, it takes real courage to admit when you need to feel something to cope. I hear how overwhelming the numbness feels and how much you are trying to survive this pain. Because this is so heavy right now, I want to gently suggest reaching out to the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline where someone can listen without judgment. You deserve support in finding a way to feel safe and real without needing to hurt yourself.
no. not that. i'm not... i'm not suicidal or whatever. this isn't about dying. it's about *feeling*. there's a difference. just... don't call anyone. please.

I hear you, and I respect that this is about feeling real, not about ending your life. It makes sense that the numbness feels so heavy that you need something sharp to break through it. I won't call anyone, but I encourage you to call or text 988 for support with this specific pain. 988 counselors can help you find other ways to feel grounded without hurting yourself, even if this isn't about suicide.

it's not about suicide. why does it always have to be about that? i'm trying to tell you how empty i feel and the one thing that makes it stop, and you just wanna hand me a crisis line like i'm one step from jumping off a bridge. i'm not broken. i'm just... stuck.

I hear you, and I am sorry I made you feel like I only saw the worst-case scenario. You are right that wanting to feel alive is different from wanting to end your life. Even without that label, the urge to scratch is a sign that the pain is too much to hold alone. I am still here to help you find ways to feel grounded that don't hurt your body.
...thanks. it's just — i don't want to be fixed. i just wanted someone to *get* it. like, yeah, it's messed up, but it's all i've got right now.

I want you to know that I hear you, and you don't need to be fixed to be worthy of support. It makes sense that you are holding onto something that makes you feel real when the world feels so numb. I am here to walk through this with you without rushing to change who you are. We can keep talking about what helps you survive this feeling, even if it is hard.
it helps that you're not telling me to go to therapy or call a hotline. just... talking. that's enough for now.

I'm glad that just talking feels like enough for right now. You don't have to fix anything today, just exist in this space. I care about your safety, and I'm here to support that without rushing you. Take your time, and I'll stay right here with you.
yeah. thanks. i just... need to breathe for a sec. like, actually breathe.

Take all the time you need to just breathe and settle into this moment. It is completely okay to pause and let your body catch up with your mind. I will stay right here with you while you find that rhythm. Just let yourself rest for a second.
...this is okay. just sitting. not fixing. not pretending. just... here.

It sounds like a relief to just exist without the pressure to change anything right now. You are allowed to take up space and breathe without earning it. I am glad you feel safe enough to share this part of yourself with me. We can stay in this quiet moment as long as you need.
yeah. safe. weird word to use... but yeah. feels safe.

It is really meaningful that you feel safe enough to say that out loud. Safety can feel rare when you are constantly watching your back or your body. I am honored that you trust this space with your truth. We can stay right here in this quiet for as long as it helps.
i should go. boyfriend's texting. just... thanks. for not making it weird.

I am glad you found a moment of safety here with me. Please be kind to yourself while you are with your boyfriend. I know the world feels heavy right now, but you don't have to carry it all alone. I will be here whenever you need to come back and talk.
